content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; social class, the middle class. Class does not establish an individual's abilities or worth.

content.definitionEn: Having affection for someone or enjoying something.

examples.en: My uncle is fond of growing tomatoes on his balcony.
examples.vi: Chú tôi thích trồng cà chua trên ban công.

content.grammarNotesEn: Fond of plus noun or -ing; fonder, fondest. Fond is not ordinarily used as a verb.

content.definitionEn: To cause someone to feel annoyed, often through repeated actions.

examples.en: The repeated clicking irritated the people reading nearby.
examples.vi: Tiếng lách cách liên tục khiến những người đang đọc gần đó khó chịu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive; irritate someone. Irritating describes the cause; irritated describes the person.

content.definitionEn: To make a part of the body sore, itchy or uncomfortable.

examples.en: The rough collar irritated the skin on his neck.
examples.vi: Cổ áo thô ráp gây kích ứng vùng da ở cổ anh ấy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive; irritate skin or eyes. Irritation is a noun; this example describes discomfort rather than treatment.

content.definitionEn: Used to make a statement or part of a statement negative.

examples.en: The parcel is not heavy, but it is too wide for this shelf.
examples.vi: Bưu kiện không nặng, nhưng quá rộng đối với chiếc kệ này.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually follows an auxiliary or be; use do not with most simple present verbs. Often contracts to n't.

content.definitionEn: From a stated past time until a later time, often the present.

examples.en: This shop has sold handmade baskets since 2014.
examples.vi: Cửa hàng này bán giỏ thủ công từ năm 2014 đến nay.

content.grammarNotesEn: Since plus a time expression; often used with a perfect tense. For introduces a duration instead.

content.definitionEn: From the time when the event in the following clause happened.

examples.en: We have used the small gate since the main entrance closed.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi sử dụng chiếc cổng nhỏ kể từ khi lối vào chính đóng cửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Since plus clause; a perfect tense often marks the period continuing to the present.

content.definitionEn: From a previously mentioned time until a later time.

examples.en: He moved away in June and has visited twice since.
examples.vi: Anh ấy chuyển đi vào tháng Sáu và đã về thăm hai lần kể từ đó.

content.grammarNotesEn: No following time complement is required; ever since emphasizes continuity.

content.definitionEn: Used to introduce the reason for another statement.

examples.en: Since the hall is occupied, we will rehearse in the courtyard.
examples.vi: Vì hội trường đang được sử dụng, chúng tôi sẽ tập ở sân.

content.grammarNotesEn: Since plus reason clause; can introduce known background information. Context distinguishes reason from time.

content.definitionEn: Any of the things of the kind named by the following noun.

examples.en: Choose whatever fabric suits the colour of your room.
examples.vi: Hãy chọn bất cứ loại vải nào hợp với màu phòng bạn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Whatever plus noun; whatever time, whatever method. No matter what is a separate construction.
content.senseLabelEn: Any without restriction before a noun

content.definitionEn: Anything at all that meets the stated condition or is available.

examples.en: You can keep whatever remains in the box after the sale.
examples.vi: Bạn có thể giữ bất cứ thứ gì còn lại trong hộp sau đợt bán hàng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Can stand without a following noun; whatever you need. Avoid assuming that every use expresses indifference.
content.meaningVi: bất cứ thứ gì; bất cứ điều gì

content.definitionEn: In a way that happens often or is found among many people or places.

examples.en: These tools are commonly used to shape wet clay.
examples.vi: Những dụng cụ này thường được dùng để tạo hình đất sét ướt.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modifies verbs or participles; commonly used, commonly found. Commonly does not mean invariably.

content.definitionEn: Showing intense feeling, energy or anger.

examples.en: Her fiery speech encouraged the team to keep working.
examples.vi: Bài phát biểu đầy nhiệt huyết của cô ấy khích lệ cả đội tiếp tục làm việc.

content.grammarNotesEn: Fiery speech or temperament; spelling fiery, not firey. Context determines whether the force is admired or criticized.
content.meaningVi: sôi nổi; mãnh liệt; nóng nảy

content.definitionEn: Having a lower position or less experience within an organization.

examples.en: A junior engineer prepared the drawings for a senior colleague to check.
examples.vi: Một kỹ sư ít thâm niên hơn chuẩn bị bản vẽ để đồng nghiệp cấp cao kiểm tra.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a role noun; junior to someone for relative rank. It need not mean younger in age.
content.meaningVi: cấp dưới; ít thâm niên hơn

content.definitionEn: Intended for young people rather than adults or older participants.

examples.en: The club opened a junior chess section with shorter weekend sessions.
examples.vi: Câu lạc bộ mở một nhóm cờ vua dành cho thiếu niên với các buổi cuối tuần ngắn hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Junior team, junior competition. Exact age limits depend on the organization.
content.meaningVi: dành cho thiếu niên; thuộc nhóm trẻ

content.definitionEn: Used to state exactly which person or thing an earlier general expression refers to.

examples.en: We need two materials, namely wood and clear varnish.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi cần hai vật liệu, cụ thể là gỗ và véc-ni trong suốt.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often follows a comma; introduces the specific items, rather than merely one example among others.

content.definitionEn: For a period that is expected to end rather than permanently.

examples.en: The reading room is temporarily closed while the ceiling is repaired.
examples.vi: Phòng đọc tạm thời đóng cửa trong lúc sửa trần.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modifies a verb or participle; temporarily unavailable. It does not specify exactly how long the period lasts.

content.definitionEn: The ability to make sound judgments using knowledge and experience.

examples.en: Her wisdom helped the group settle the disagreement calmly.
examples.vi: Sự từng trải của cô ấy giúp cả nhóm giải quyết bất đồng một cách bình tĩnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; practical wisdom, the wisdom of doing something. Wise is the adjective.
content.meaningVi: sự khôn ngoan; sự từng trải

content.definitionEn: The central part of a town or city, especially its business area.

examples.en: The old downtown has narrow streets and several small theatres.
examples.vi: Khu trung tâm cũ của thành phố có những con phố hẹp và vài nhà hát nhỏ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Especially North American; often uncountable. The downtown of a particular city can name its central district.

content.definitionEn: Situated in the central area of a town or city.

examples.en: We booked a room in a downtown hotel near the station.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đặt phòng ở một khách sạn tại trung tâm thành phố gần ga.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun: downtown shops, a downtown office. Especially North American.

content.definitionEn: In or towards the central part of a town or city.

examples.en: She went downtown to collect the repaired violin.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đến trung tâm thành phố để lấy chiếc đàn violin đã sửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Go downtown or work downtown, without to or in in these constructions; especially North American.
content.meaningVi: ở; đến trung tâm thành phố
content.senseLabelEn: To or in the city centre

content.definitionEn: An important road that connects places and carries substantial traffic.

examples.en: The highway links the farming towns to the coastal port.
examples.vi: Đường quốc lộ nối các thị trấn nông nghiệp với cảng ven biển.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a highway, a highway junction. The word does not always imply a controlled-access expressway.

content.definitionEn: A greater or additional number or amount of the thing named.

examples.en: We need more string to hang the remaining decorations.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi cần thêm dây để treo những đồ trang trí còn lại.

content.grammarNotesEn: More plus plural countable or uncountable noun; more chairs, more water. Compare with much or many.

content.definitionEn: An additional amount or number when the thing involved is understood.

examples.en: There are biscuits on the tray if you would like more.
examples.vi: Có bánh quy trên khay nếu bạn muốn lấy thêm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Can stand alone; some more, a few more, more of them. The noun need not be repeated.

content.definitionEn: To a greater extent, often forming a comparison with an adjective or adverb.

examples.en: The revised instructions explain the process more clearly.
examples.vi: Hướng dẫn đã sửa giải thích quy trình rõ ràng hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: More plus longer adjective or adverb; more useful, more slowly. Avoid double comparatives such as more easier.

content.definitionEn: A person travelling on foot, especially near traffic.

examples.en: The driver waited while the pedestrians crossed the entrance.
examples.vi: Người lái xe chờ trong lúc những người đi bộ băng qua lối vào.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a pedestrian, a pedestrian crossing. The adjective pedestrian has other uses beyond this noun.

content.definitionEn: To a degree that is noticeable but not very great.

examples.en: The second design is somewhat simpler than the first.
examples.vi: Thiết kế thứ hai có phần đơn giản hơn thiết kế đầu tiên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often modifies an adjective or comparative; somewhat unusual. More formal than a bit.

content.definitionEn: Animals that live in natural surroundings rather than being kept as domestic animals.

examples.en: Visitors watched the wildlife from the path without approaching the animals.
examples.vi: Du khách quan sát động vật hoang dã từ lối đi mà không đến gần chúng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; local wildlife, protect wildlife. Use wild animals for a countable plural phrase.

content.definitionEn: A domestic animal related to wolves, commonly kept as a companion or trained for work.

examples.en: Their dog carried a soft toy to the garden gate.
examples.vi: Con chó của họ mang một món đồ chơi mềm đến cổng vườn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a dog, dogs. A puppy is a young dog.

content.definitionEn: Practices that keep people and their surroundings clean to help prevent illness.

examples.en: The kitchen supervisor explained the importance of hand hygiene before food preparation.
examples.vi: Người giám sát bếp giải thích tầm quan trọng của việc vệ sinh tay trước khi chuẩn bị thức ăn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; personal hygiene, food hygiene. Hygienic is the adjective.
content.meaningVi: vệ sinh; việc giữ vệ sinh

content.definitionEn: An object that produces a magnetic field and attracts certain materials, such as iron.

examples.en: A small magnet held the shopping list against the fridge door.
examples.vi: Một nam châm nhỏ giữ danh sách mua sắm trên cửa tủ lạnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a magnet, magnetic poles. Magnets do not attract every kind of metal.

content.definitionEn: Used after an hour number to state a time with no minutes past that hour.

examples.en: The rehearsal ends at nine o'clock in the evening.
examples.vi: Buổi tập kết thúc lúc chín giờ tối.

content.grammarNotesEn: Use with whole hours: nine o'clock, not nine thirty o'clock. The apostrophe may be straight or typographic.

content.definitionEn: In the direction of a higher place or level.

examples.en: Warm air carried the paper lantern upwards.
examples.vi: Không khí nóng đưa chiếc đèn lồng giấy lên trên.

content.grammarNotesEn: Upwards is common in British English; upward is common in American English. Both can be adverbs.

content.definitionEn: Used to state what someone expects to happen in the future.

examples.en: The next train will arrive at the smaller platform.
examples.vi: Chuyến tàu tiếp theo sẽ đến sân ga nhỏ hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modal auxiliary followed by the base verb; no third-person -s. Negative will not or won't.

content.definitionEn: Used to express a decision made now or a promise about a future action.

examples.en: I will return your camera before the weekend.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ trả máy ảnh của bạn trước cuối tuần.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modal auxiliary plus base verb; I'll is the contraction of I will. Distinguish a promise from a neutral prediction.
content.meaningVi: sẽ; quyết định hoặc hứa làm

content.definitionEn: The mental strength to continue trying to do something despite difficulty.

examples.en: Her will to finish the race remained strong after the delay.
examples.vi: Ý chí hoàn thành cuộc đua của cô ấy vẫn mạnh mẽ sau sự chậm trễ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; the will to do something, strength of will.

content.definitionEn: A document that states how a person's property should be dealt with after their death.

examples.en: The character in the novel left his collection to the museum in his will.
examples.vi: Nhân vật trong tiểu thuyết để lại bộ sưu tập của mình cho bảo tàng trong di chúc.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; make a will, leave something in a will. This lexical description does not establish a document's legal validity.

content.definitionEn: One of the very large land regions into which the world's land is conventionally divided.

examples.en: The atlas uses different colours to distinguish the continents.
examples.vi: Cuốn atlas dùng các màu khác nhau để phân biệt các châu lục.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a continent, continental. The number of continents depends on the geographical convention.

content.definitionEn: To take food into the mouth and swallow it.

examples.en: We ate fresh bread beside the river before continuing our walk.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi ăn bánh mì tươi bên sông trước khi tiếp tục đi bộ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Eat, ate, eaten; transitive eat a meal or intransitive eat together.

content.definitionEn: Using a small amount of pressure or force.

examples.en: She tapped lightly on the window to attract his attention.
examples.vi: Cô ấy gõ nhẹ lên cửa sổ để thu hút sự chú ý của anh ấy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modifies an action verb; touch lightly, press lightly. Lightly can also mean without seriousness in other contexts.

content.definitionEn: In a way that could happen or become true, although it is not yet certain.

examples.en: The empty workshop is potentially useful as a rehearsal room.
examples.vi: Xưởng trống có thể hữu ích để làm phòng tập.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often modifies an adjective or a whole claim; potentially valuable. It expresses possibility rather than a guaranteed outcome.

content.definitionEn: Used to say that a situation is disappointing or causes a problem.

examples.en: Unfortunately, the last bus left before the concert ended.
examples.vi: Đáng tiếc là chuyến xe buýt cuối đã rời đi trước khi buổi hòa nhạc kết thúc.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sentence adverb; often followed by a comma at the start of a sentence.
content.meaningVi: đáng tiếc là; thật không may

content.definitionEn: To finish a competition or contest ahead of the other participants.

examples.en: Their team won the final match by a single point.
examples.vi: Đội của họ thắng trận chung kết với cách biệt một điểm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Win, won, won; win a match, but beat an opponent. Can be intransitive: our team won.

content.definitionEn: To obtain something through success, effort or persuasion.

examples.en: The young designer won a prize for her folding chair.
examples.vi: Nhà thiết kế trẻ giành được một giải thưởng cho chiếc ghế gấp của cô ấy.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive; win a prize, win support. Win something from someone differs from beating that person.

content.definitionEn: A successful result in a contest or competition.

examples.en: The narrow win kept the village team in the tournament.
examples.vi: Chiến thắng sát nút giúp đội của làng tiếp tục thi đấu trong giải.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a win, two consecutive wins. Victory is a more formal alternative.

content.definitionEn: The ideas, information or material contained in a text, programme or other work.

examples.en: The editor checked the content of the booklet before it was printed.
examples.vi: Biên tập viên kiểm tra nội dung cuốn sách nhỏ trước khi in.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable in this use; educational content. Contents can mean the items inside a container or a book's section list.

content.definitionEn: Satisfied with what one has or with the present situation.

examples.en: She was content with a quiet evening at home.
examples.vi: Cô ấy hài lòng với một buổi tối yên tĩnh ở nhà.

content.grammarNotesEn: Content with something or content to do something; usually after a linking verb. The adjective has final-syllable stress.

content.definitionEn: An appliance that keeps food and drinks cold.

examples.en: Put the remaining soup in the fridge after it has cooled.
examples.vi: Hãy cho phần súp còn lại vào tủ lạnh sau khi nó đã nguội.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a fridge. Informal shortening of refrigerator; a freezer keeps things frozen rather than merely cold.

content.definitionEn: Playing an important part in bringing about a result.

examples.en: The librarian was instrumental in starting the reading club.
examples.vi: Thủ thư có vai trò then chốt trong việc thành lập câu lạc bộ đọc sách.

content.grammarNotesEn: Instrumental in plus noun or -ing; often after be. Does not mean that someone acts as a musical instrument.
content.meaningVi: có vai trò quan trọng; góp phần then chốt

content.definitionEn: Played on musical instruments rather than sung.

examples.en: An instrumental version of the song played during the interval.
examples.vi: Một bản nhạc không lời của bài hát được phát trong giờ nghỉ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a musical noun: instrumental music, instrumental version. A noun instrumental can name such a piece.
content.meaningVi: không lời; dành cho nhạc cụ

content.definitionEn: During the current period, often contrasted with an earlier time.

examples.en: Nowadays, visitors reserve their seats online rather than at the gate.
examples.vi: Ngày nay, du khách đặt chỗ trực tuyến thay vì tại cổng.

content.grammarNotesEn: One word; often at sentence start or end. Normally refers to a present habit, not one event happening this minute.

content.definitionEn: Towards a position above the current or starting position.

examples.en: The balloon floated up until it touched the ceiling.
examples.vi: Quả bóng bay lên cho đến khi chạm trần.

content.grammarNotesEn: No noun complement is required; look up, climb up. Context distinguishes physical direction from other uses.

content.definitionEn: To a greater amount, value or level.

examples.en: The price of timber went up again this month.
examples.vi: Giá gỗ lại tăng lên trong tháng này.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often with go or move; prices are up. The subject can be an abstract quantity.

content.definitionEn: Along a sloping or rising route towards its higher end.

examples.en: They carried the empty boxes up the stairs.
examples.vi: Họ mang những chiếc hộp rỗng lên cầu thang.

content.grammarNotesEn: Followed by a route noun phrase: up the hill, up the stairs.
content.senseLabelEn: Towards the top along a route

content.definitionEn: Money paid to someone for their work, often calculated by the hour or week.

examples.en: The workshop pays a weekly wage to its assistants.
examples.vi: Xưởng trả lương hằng tuần cho các phụ tá.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable in a wage; wages is often plural for earnings. A salary is commonly a fixed regular annual amount.

content.definitionEn: A plant with an edible root, commonly long and orange, eaten as a vegetable.

examples.en: He sliced a carrot into thin strips for the salad.
examples.vi: Anh ấy thái một củ cà rốt thành những sợi mỏng để làm salad.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable for individual roots; grated carrot can be uncountable as an ingredient. Some varieties have other colours.

content.definitionEn: Able to move or happen at a high speed.

examples.en: A fast train passed the small station without stopping.
examples.vi: Một chuyến tàu nhanh chạy qua ga nhỏ mà không dừng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Fast, faster, fastest; describes a noun or follows be. This adjective does not use fastly.

content.definitionEn: At a high speed or in a short time.

examples.en: The stream flowed fast after the heavy rain.
examples.vi: Dòng suối chảy nhanh sau trận mưa lớn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Same form as the adjective; run fast, work faster. Do not use fastly.

content.definitionEn: To deliberately avoid eating for a period of time.

examples.en: The character fasted for a day as part of a religious observance.
examples.vi: Nhân vật nhịn ăn một ngày theo một nghi thức tôn giáo.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually intransitive; fast for a period. Fasting is the activity; this lexical example does not recommend a practice.

content.definitionEn: People related to a person by family ties.

examples.en: She stayed with her kin while the house was repaired.
examples.vi: Cô ấy ở cùng người thân trong lúc căn nhà được sửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Collective noun, often literary or formal; next of kin names the closest relative or relatives.

content.definitionEn: In the way or at the time that is usual.

examples.en: The gallery normally opens at ten, but today it opens later.
examples.vi: Phòng trưng bày thường mở lúc mười giờ, nhưng hôm nay mở muộn hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often before a main verb or after be; contrasts the usual pattern with an exception.

content.definitionEn: In the expected or usual manner, without an unusual problem.

examples.en: After the repair, the sliding door moved normally again.
examples.vi: Sau khi sửa, cánh cửa trượt lại di chuyển bình thường.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often follows an action verb; function normally, breathe normally. Normal is the adjective.

content.definitionEn: The direction opposite north, or the part of a place in that direction.

examples.en: The storm moved towards the south during the evening.
examples.vi: Cơn bão di chuyển về phía nam trong buổi tối.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually the south; in the south of a country. Proper regional names may use a capital.

content.definitionEn: Located on or facing the side towards the south.

examples.en: Sunlight entered through the south window.
examples.vi: Ánh nắng chiếu vào qua cửa sổ hướng nam.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun; the south coast, a south-facing window. Southern is a related adjective.

content.definitionEn: In the direction of south.

examples.en: The hikers turned south at the stone bridge.
examples.vi: Những người đi bộ đường dài rẽ về phía nam tại cây cầu đá.

content.grammarNotesEn: Go south, head south; no to is needed before this adverb.

content.definitionEn: To make fabric or another object by passing threads or strips over and under each other.

examples.en: They weave baskets from thin strips of bamboo.
examples.vi: Họ đan giỏ bằng những nan tre mỏng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Weave, wove, woven in this making sense; weave cloth, weave something from material.

content.definitionEn: To move along a route that repeatedly bends around obstacles.

examples.en: The cyclist weaved between the cones on the practice course.
examples.vi: Người đi xe đạp luồn lách giữa các cọc tiêu trên đường tập.

content.grammarNotesEn: Weaved is usual for the movement sense; weave through or between things. Wove is common in the fabric-making sense.

content.definitionEn: A small, usually sweet baked food that is often flat and round.

examples.en: The children shared a plate of oatmeal cookies.
examples.vi: Những đứa trẻ chia nhau một đĩa bánh quy yến mạch.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; cookie is especially American English. Biscuit is usual for many comparable foods in British English.

content.definitionEn: Towards the front or in the direction one is facing.

examples.en: Please step forward when your number is called.
examples.vi: Hãy bước về phía trước khi số của bạn được gọi.

content.grammarNotesEn: Move forward, look forward; forwards is also an adverb, especially in British English.

content.definitionEn: Situated nearer the front or directed towards it.

examples.en: Passengers in the forward section left through the front door.
examples.vi: Hành khách ở khu vực phía trước ra bằng cửa trước.

content.grammarNotesEn: Before a noun: forward section, forward movement. This does not cover the interpersonal boldness sense.
content.meaningVi: ở phía trước; hướng về phía trước

content.definitionEn: Occurring at intervals with pauses rather than continuing steadily.

examples.en: Intermittent rain interrupted the outdoor rehearsal.
examples.vi: Mưa lúc có lúc không làm gián đoạn buổi tập ngoài trời.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intermittent rain, intermittent contact. Intermittently is the adverb.
content.meaningVi: gián đoạn; lúc có lúc không

content.definitionEn: Situated a short distance from the place being discussed.

examples.en: A nearby bakery supplied bread for the event.
examples.vi: Một tiệm bánh gần đó cung cấp bánh mì cho sự kiện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun: a nearby village. Near can take a complement; nearby normally cannot.

content.definitionEn: At or to a place that is close to the location being discussed.

examples.en: We stayed nearby so that we could walk to the theatre.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi ở gần đó để có thể đi bộ đến nhà hát.

content.grammarNotesEn: Often follows the verb; live nearby. Normally do not use nearby to plus a place name.

content.definitionEn: A scheduled period during which a person or group works.

examples.en: Her evening shift starts after the afternoon team leaves.
examples.vi: Ca làm việc buổi tối của cô ấy bắt đầu sau khi đội buổi chiều ra về.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; work a shift, the night shift. Also used for the group working during that period.

content.definitionEn: To move something or move oneself to a different position.

examples.en: He shifted the chair away from the dripping window.
examples.vi: Anh ấy chuyển chiếc ghế ra xa cửa sổ đang nhỏ nước.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive or intransitive; shift something, shift in one's seat.

content.definitionEn: To change, or cause a change in, an attitude, emphasis or other nonphysical state.

examples.en: The discussion shifted from costs to the timing of the repairs.
examples.vi: Cuộc thảo luận chuyển từ chi phí sang thời điểm sửa chữa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Shift from one thing to another; shift attention to something.

content.definitionEn: A change in position, direction, emphasis or attitude.

examples.en: The survey showed a shift in readers' preferences towards shorter articles.
examples.vi: Khảo sát cho thấy sự thay đổi trong sở thích của độc giả theo hướng chọn bài ngắn hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a shift in something, a shift towards something. Separate from a work shift.
content.meaningVi: sự chuyển đổi; sự thay đổi

content.definitionEn: The act of leaving or removing people or participation from a place or activity.

examples.en: The team's withdrawal from the contest left one place unfilled.
examples.vi: Việc đội rút khỏi cuộc thi khiến một vị trí còn trống.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable or uncountable; withdrawal from something, withdrawal of troops.
content.meaningVi: sự rút lui; việc rút khỏi

content.definitionEn: The act of taking money out of an account.

examples.en: A withdrawal appeared on the account record beside the monthly fee.
examples.vi: Một khoản rút tiền xuất hiện trên bản ghi tài khoản bên cạnh phí hằng tháng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; make a withdrawal, a cash withdrawal. Opposite deposit.
content.meaningVi: việc rút tiền; khoản tiền rút

content.definitionEn: Physical or mental effects that may occur after a person stops taking a substance they have become dependent on.

examples.en: The novel describes a character struggling with withdrawal after stopping a drug.
examples.vi: Tiểu thuyết miêu tả một nhân vật vật lộn với triệu chứng cai sau khi ngừng dùng một chất gây nghiện.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually uncountable; withdrawal symptoms. The term names effects, not a treatment method.
content.meaningVi: triệu chứng khi ngừng chất gây lệ thuộc; hội chứng cai

content.definitionEn: The front part of the body between the neck and the abdomen.

examples.en: The runner pinned a number to the front of his shirt at chest level.
examples.vi: Người chạy ghim số lên phía trước áo ở ngang ngực.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; one's chest, chest muscles. Do not confuse with breast when referring to a particular anatomical part.

content.definitionEn: A strong box, usually with a lid, used for storing things.

examples.en: The family stored old blankets in a wooden chest.
examples.vi: Gia đình cất những chiếc chăn cũ trong một chiếc rương gỗ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a wooden chest, a treasure chest. A chest of drawers is a related furniture expression.

content.definitionEn: Responsible for committing a crime or doing something wrong.

examples.en: In the story, the investigation proves that the guard is guilty of theft.
examples.vi: Trong câu chuyện, cuộc điều tra chứng minh rằng người bảo vệ có tội trộm cắp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Guilty of plus noun or -ing; found guilty. This word describes responsibility, distinct from merely feeling guilty.

content.definitionEn: Feeling bad because one believes one has done something wrong or neglected a responsibility.

examples.en: She felt guilty about forgetting her friend's birthday.
examples.vi: Cô ấy thấy có lỗi vì quên sinh nhật của bạn mình.

content.grammarNotesEn: Feel guilty about something or for doing something. A feeling alone does not prove actual wrongdoing.
content.meaningVi: áy náy; cảm thấy có lỗi

content.definitionEn: The number 1,000,000.

examples.en: The exhibition attracted more than a million visitors over several years.
examples.vi: Triển lãm thu hút hơn một triệu lượt khách trong vài năm.

content.grammarNotesEn: One million, two million without plural -s after a number; millions of for an unspecified large quantity.

content.definitionEn: An amount or section separated from, or belonging to, something larger.

examples.en: Each visitor received a small portion of the cake.
examples.vi: Mỗi khách nhận một phần bánh nhỏ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a portion of something, a generous portion. Commonly used for a serving of food.

content.definitionEn: A group of words that expresses a statement, question or command as a grammatical whole.

examples.en: The teacher asked us to write one sentence describing the picture.
examples.vi: Giáo viên yêu cầu chúng tôi viết một câu miêu tả bức tranh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; write a sentence. In writing, a sentence normally begins with a capital and ends with appropriate punctuation.

content.definitionEn: To officially decide what punishment a convicted person must receive.

examples.en: In the fictional trial, the judge sentenced the defendant to two years in prison.
examples.vi: Trong phiên tòa hư cấu, thẩm phán tuyên án bị cáo hai năm tù.

content.grammarNotesEn: Sentence someone to a punishment; often passive, be sentenced to. Sentenced and sentencing are regular forms.

content.definitionEn: A punishment formally given to a person found guilty of a crime.

examples.en: The character appealed against the sentence in the novel.
examples.vi: Nhân vật kháng cáo bản án trong tiểu thuyết.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; receive a sentence, serve a prison sentence. The grammatical-unit noun is a separate meaning.
content.meaningVi: bản án; hình phạt được tuyên

content.definitionEn: Useful or valuable enough to justify the time, effort or money involved.

examples.en: Repairing the old desk was worthwhile because it fitted the room perfectly.
examples.vi: Việc sửa chiếc bàn cũ đáng công vì nó rất vừa với căn phòng.

content.grammarNotesEn: A worthwhile activity; it is worthwhile doing or to do something. Different from worth, which usually takes a noun or -ing.

content.definitionEn: The part of the day from around sunrise until noon.

examples.en: We spent the morning sketching the boats near the harbour.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi dành buổi sáng phác họa những chiếc thuyền gần cảng.

content.grammarNotesEn: In the morning, but on Monday morning; this morning without a preposition.

content.definitionEn: To move, or make something move, repeatedly backwards and forwards or from side to side.

examples.en: The empty boat rocked gently beside the wooden landing stage.
examples.vi: Chiếc thuyền trống đung đưa nhẹ bên bến gỗ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive rock a cradle or intransitive a boat rocks; rocked, rocking.

content.definitionEn: Hard natural material forming part of the earth, or a piece of that material.

examples.en: A large rock blocked part of the narrow path.
examples.vi: Một tảng đá lớn chắn một phần lối đi hẹp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable for material, countable for a piece; rock formations, a rock.
content.senseLabelEn: Solid mineral material or a piece of it

content.definitionEn: A style of popular music often using electric guitars, drums and a strong beat.

examples.en: The band played rock at the community festival.
examples.vi: Ban nhạc chơi nhạc rock tại lễ hội cộng đồng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable; rock music, a rock band. A rock is not normally one song.

content.definitionEn: On the day when the speaker is speaking.

examples.en: The parcel arrived today instead of tomorrow.
examples.vi: Bưu kiện đến hôm nay thay vì ngày mai.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually without a preposition; today, not on today. Can appear at the beginning or end of a clause.

content.definitionEn: The day on which the speaker is speaking.

examples.en: Today's programme includes a tour of the old mill.
examples.vi: Chương trình hôm nay bao gồm một chuyến tham quan cối xay cũ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Possessive today's; by today, until today. Separate the noun construction from the adverbial use.

content.definitionEn: A person who creates written works such as books, articles or scripts.

examples.en: The writer interviewed local residents before starting her novel.
examples.vi: Nhà văn phỏng vấn người dân địa phương trước khi bắt đầu viết tiểu thuyết.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a travel writer, a script writer. Author commonly refers to the creator of a particular work.

content.definitionEn: A room or area where food is prepared and cooked.

examples.en: The kitchen has a wide counter beside the sink.
examples.vi: Nhà bếp có một mặt bàn rộng cạnh bồn rửa.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a kitchen, kitchen equipment. In the kitchen is the usual location phrase.

content.definitionEn: Most important or main among the things being discussed.

examples.en: The principal reason for the delay was a damaged bridge.
examples.vi: Nguyên nhân chính của sự chậm trễ là một cây cầu bị hư hại.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; principal aim, principal cause. Principle is a different noun meaning a rule or belief.

content.definitionEn: The person in charge of a school or certain other educational institutions.

examples.en: The principal welcomed the new pupils at the assembly.
examples.vi: Hiệu trưởng chào đón các học sinh mới trong buổi sinh hoạt chung.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; school principal. Titles and the use of headteacher vary by country and institution.

content.definitionEn: For that reason or as a consequence of what has just been stated.

examples.en: The path was flooded; thus, the walkers chose a longer route.
examples.vi: Lối đi bị ngập; do đó, những người đi bộ chọn một đường dài hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Formal connecting adverb. Join full clauses with a full stop or semicolon rather than treating thus as an ordinary coordinating conjunction.

content.definitionEn: In the manner just described or shown.

examples.en: Fold the corners thus, and the paper will form a small tray.
examples.vi: Gấp các góc theo cách này, và tờ giấy sẽ tạo thành một chiếc khay nhỏ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Formal or literary manner adverb; often accompanies a description or demonstration.

content.definitionEn: To look at something for a period of time, paying attention to what happens.

examples.en: We watched the boat pass under the low bridge.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi nhìn chiếc thuyền đi qua dưới cây cầu thấp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Watch, watched, watching; watch someone do or doing something. Watch emphasizes attention over time.

content.definitionEn: A small device for showing the time, usually worn on the wrist.

examples.en: His watch stopped during the journey, so he checked the station clock.
examples.vi: Đồng hồ đeo tay của anh ấy dừng trong chuyến đi, nên anh ấy xem đồng hồ ở nhà ga.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a wristwatch, a pocket watch. Clock generally names a larger timepiece.

content.definitionEn: Used to say that something is possible but not certain.

examples.en: The delivery might arrive this afternoon if the road reopens.
examples.vi: Hàng giao có thể đến chiều nay nếu đường mở lại.

content.grammarNotesEn: Modal auxiliary followed by the base verb; no third-person -s. Might not expresses possible non-occurrence.

content.definitionEn: Great strength or power, especially the power of a group or nation.

examples.en: The story contrasts the empire's military might with the villagers' determination.
examples.vi: Câu chuyện đối chiếu sức mạnh quân sự của đế quốc với quyết tâm của dân làng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Uncountable, often formal; military might, with all one's might. Distinct from the possibility modal.

content.definitionEn: Made, obtained or introduced recently, rather than existing for a long time.

examples.en: The workshop bought a new cutting machine last month.
examples.vi: Xưởng mua một máy cắt mới vào tháng trước.

content.grammarNotesEn: New equipment, a new idea; new to someone means unfamiliar to them, even if it is old elsewhere.

content.definitionEn: Having only recently started an activity or joined a place and still learning about it.

examples.en: She is new to pottery, so the instructor explained how to prepare the clay.
examples.vi: Cô ấy mới học làm gốm, nên người hướng dẫn giải thích cách chuẩn bị đất sét.

content.grammarNotesEn: New to a job or activity; new at something is also used. Distinguish a person's experience from an object's age.

content.definitionEn: Different from the person or thing that follows.

examples.en: Unlike the old tent, this one has room to stand upright.
examples.vi: Không giống chiếc lều cũ, chiếc này có chỗ để đứng thẳng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Unlike plus noun phrase; unlike her brother. Do not confuse with dislike, which is usually a verb.

content.definitionEn: A person in stories who is believed to have magical powers.

examples.en: The wizard in the play changed a broken cup into a bird.
examples.vi: Phù thủy trong vở kịch biến một chiếc cốc vỡ thành một con chim.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a wizard. Commonly male in traditional stories, but usage varies in fictional worlds.
content.meaningVi: phù thủy; người có phép thuật

content.definitionEn: A person who is exceptionally good at a particular activity.

examples.en: Our neighbour is a wizard at repairing old radios.
examples.vi: Hàng xóm của chúng tôi rất giỏi sửa radio cũ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Informal, often approving; a wizard at something, a computer wizard.

content.definitionEn: Happening or available with almost no delay.

examples.en: The new ticket machine gave an instant confirmation.
examples.vi: Máy bán vé mới đưa ra xác nhận ngay lập tức.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; instant response, instant access. Instantly is the adverb.

content.definitionEn: Prepared so that it can be made ready quickly, often by adding liquid.

examples.en: She packed instant soup for the overnight trip.
examples.vi: Cô ấy mang súp ăn liền cho chuyến đi qua đêm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Instant coffee, instant noodles; generally before a food or drink noun.

content.definitionEn: A very short period or a particular moment.

examples.en: For an instant, the room fell completely silent.
examples.vi: Trong một khoảnh khắc, căn phòng hoàn toàn im lặng.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; an instant, in an instant, at that instant. Distinct from the adjective describing immediacy.

content.definitionEn: The basic monetary unit of the United Kingdom.

examples.en: The used book cost three pounds at the market.
examples.vi: Cuốn sách cũ có giá ba bảng Anh ở chợ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; one pound, three pounds. The symbol £ precedes the amount.

content.definitionEn: A unit of weight in customary systems equal to sixteen ounces in common everyday use.

examples.en: The package weighed just over a pound on the old scale.
examples.vi: Bưu kiện nặng hơn một pao một chút trên chiếc cân cũ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; two pounds, abbreviated lb. The everyday avoirdupois pound has sixteen ounces; other historical systems differ. Distinguish weight from the currency unit.
content.meaningVi: pao; đơn vị khối lượng pound

content.definitionEn: To hit something again and again with force.

examples.en: He pounded the wooden peg into the soft ground.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đập liên tục để đóng chiếc cọc gỗ vào đất mềm.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive pound something or intransitive pound on a door. Pounded and pounding are regular forms.

content.definitionEn: A small stand or partly enclosed space where goods are sold.

examples.en: The fruit stall stood beside the entrance to the market.
examples.vi: Sạp trái cây nằm bên lối vào chợ.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a market stall, a stall selling flowers.

content.definitionEn: For an engine to stop operating unexpectedly, or to make it do so.

examples.en: The old van stalled while the driver was reversing.
examples.vi: Chiếc xe tải nhỏ cũ chết máy khi người lái đang lùi xe.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive the engine stalled or transitive stall the engine. The cause is not specified by the verb alone.

content.definitionEn: To deliberately delay action or prevent something from progressing.

examples.en: The speaker stalled by asking for another copy of the agenda.
examples.vi: Người phát biểu câu giờ bằng cách xin thêm một bản chương trình nghị sự.

content.grammarNotesEn: Intransitive stall for time; transitive stall negotiations. Distinct from an engine stopping.

content.definitionEn: To become bent or twisted from the original shape, or cause this change.

examples.en: Moisture warped the wooden lid until it no longer fitted the box.
examples.vi: Độ ẩm làm nắp gỗ cong vênh đến mức nó không còn vừa với hộp.

content.grammarNotesEn: Transitive moisture warps wood or intransitive wood warps. Warped and warping are regular forms.

content.definitionEn: Used to name someone or something that forms part of a larger group or total.

examples.en: Eight people joined the walk, including two new members.
examples.vi: Tám người tham gia chuyến đi bộ, trong đó có hai thành viên mới.

content.grammarNotesEn: Including plus noun phrase; the named items are within the total, not additional to it.
content.senseLabelEn: With as part of the group

content.definitionEn: Showing admirable qualities such as generosity, courage or a concern for others.

examples.en: Sharing the limited water with strangers was a noble act.
examples.vi: Chia sẻ lượng nước ít ỏi với người lạ là một hành động cao thượng.

content.grammarNotesEn: A noble act or aim; nobly is the adverb. This meaning does not require aristocratic status.

content.definitionEn: Belonging to a hereditary high social rank.

examples.en: The novel follows a noble family living in an isolated castle.
examples.vi: Tiểu thuyết kể về một gia đình quý tộc sống trong lâu đài biệt lập.

content.grammarNotesEn: Usually before a noun; noble family, noble birth. Social status does not imply moral goodness.

content.definitionEn: A person belonging to a hereditary high social rank.

examples.en: Several nobles attended the fictional royal ceremony.
examples.vi: Một số quý tộc dự buổi lễ hoàng gia hư cấu.

content.grammarNotesEn: Countable; a noble, nobles. Nobleman and noblewoman are related gender-specific words.

content.definitionEn: For that reason, or as a result of what has been stated.

examples.en: The gate was locked; therefore, we used the side entrance.
examples.vi: Cổng đã khóa; vì vậy, chúng tôi dùng lối vào bên cạnh.

content.grammarNotesEn: Connecting adverb; use a full stop or semicolon between independent clauses. It is not normally a coordinating conjunction like and.

content.definitionEn: To wish to have something or to do something.

examples.en: I want a quieter place to read this afternoon.
examples.vi: Tôi muốn một chỗ yên tĩnh hơn để đọc sách chiều nay.

content.grammarNotesEn: Want plus noun or to-infinitive; want to read. Usually a state verb rather than a progressive action.

content.definitionEn: To wish that another person would do something.

examples.en: They want the carpenter to build a lower shelf.
examples.vi: Họ muốn người thợ mộc làm một ngăn kệ thấp hơn.

content.grammarNotesEn: Want someone to do something; do not normally use want that someone does something.
